standard.title: Collaborate using transacting, negotiating and justifying language
standard.description: collaborate in activities that involve the language of transacting, negotiating and justifying to plan events
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can plan and negotiate with others using modelled and idiomatic language, reaching agreement and resolving differences (AC9LCH6C02). They have collaborated on community-facing projects. They have not yet used justification language in collaborative planning, conducted community interviews, or led events involving external community members.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students collaborate in activities involving the language of transacting, negotiating and justifying to plan events — including community-facing activities, peer support resources, and events involving external participants.

nodes.label: Justification language in collaborative planning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use justification language — reasoning, evidence, consequence framing — to support positions and proposals in collaborative planning contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least two justification structures during a collaborative planning task — for example, giving a reason for a proposal, citing evidence for a decision, or framing a consequence.
nodes.typical_width: Use justification language — reasoning, consequence framing, evidence reference — in collaborative planning; provide metalanguage-supported feedback on peers' contributions; negotiate and justify decisions for events including place, time, program, and participants.
wider: Lead a planning discussion — facilitating justification-based decision making and managing competing proposals to a shared outcome using target language
Compare how justification is expressed in collaborative contexts in the target language with English — identify where the conventions differ in directness or formality
nodes.hinge_reason: Justification language distinguishes collaborative negotiation from simple preference exchange. Students who can only assert preferences cannot engage in the evidence-based, reasoned planning that this descriptor requires and that the Y9-10 discussion descriptors build upon.

response_modes.reason: Justification in collaborative contexts requires students to construct and deploy reasoned arguments — not just express preferences. Explicit modelling of justification structures followed by scaffolded planning tasks builds the argumentative capacity needed.

success_criteria: Uses at least two justification structures during a collaborative planning task
Supports at least one proposal with a reason or evidence

nodes.label: Community interviews and engagement
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can prepare and conduct interviews with community members in the target language, gathering information about life experience, migration, culture, or community topics.
nodes.minimum_width: Prepare at least five interview questions and conduct an interview with a community member or peer, using appropriate target language for the exchange.
nodes.typical_width: Prepare and conduct community interviews on topics such as migration, life experiences, career choices and cultural practices; use appropriate interview register and structure; gather and present findings; create resources to help others using interview data.
wider: Conduct an interview with a community elder or significant community figure — prepare culturally appropriate questions, manage the interaction respectfully, and present findings for a community audience

Compare interview conventions in the target language community with Australian English interview norms — identify differences in how rapport is built, questions are framed, and the interview is closed

response_modes.reason: Interview skills require practice across varied participants and topics — the same question forms used with a peer may not transfer appropriately to a community elder or unfamiliar adult. Varied interview contexts build flexible, register-appropriate interviewing capacity.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Community interviews are the highest-authenticity interaction context for background language learners. Width investment here — real community members, real topics — produces qualitatively different communicative experience from simulated classroom interaction, and connects students to their broader language community.
success_criteria: Prepares at least five interview questions appropriate to the context
Conducts an interview using appropriate register and structure throughout

nodes.label: Planning and executing community-facing events
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can collaborate to plan and execute a community-facing event or presentation — organising logistics, creating promotional materials, and managing the event using target language.
nodes.minimum_width: Contribute to planning and executing a community-facing event — participating in at least three planning decisions in target language and producing at least one piece of promotional or supporting material.
nodes.typical_width: Collaborate to plan community-facing events — excursions, cultural events, school performances, community outreach activities; create resources for others; produce promotional materials; manage event logistics using target language throughout the planning and execution process.
wider: Take a leadership role in a community-facing event — coordinate planning, delegate tasks, and manage the event itself using target language
Evaluate the event after completion — identify what communication was effective, what could be improved, and what was learned about using target language in a real community context

response_modes.reason: Community-facing event planning integrates justification language (node 1) and community engagement (node 2) into a sustained, real-stakes collaborative task. The teaching investment is in creating genuine community contexts — real audiences, real events — that require authentic transacting, negotiating and justifying.

success_criteria: Contributes to at least three planning decisions in target language
Produces at least one piece of promotional or supporting material appropriate to the event
